stories.brief: A Jerusalem Post consumer report says some supermarkets are offering large price gaps on the same Rosh Hashanah shopping basket, with the survey comparing holiday items across chains using Pricez data current to September 3, 2026. The article focuses on practical vocabulary for families shopping before the holiday, including prices, discounts, basket size, and how customers can save or overspend.

sources.title: Where will you find the cheapest Rosh Hashanah shopping basket?

stories.brief: The Jerusalem Post reports that supermarket chains are seeing weaker-than-usual customer traffic just two days before Rosh Hashanah, and some stores are cutting back on deep discounts to protect margins. The story is useful for everyday language about holiday shopping, traffic in stores, promotions, prices, and the way travel plans can change local consumer behavior.

sources.title: Ahead of the holiday: Shoppers are not rushing yet, but supermarket prices are already rising

translations.ru: В супермаркете покупателей меньше обычного, и две сети уже сокращают большие скидки.
translations.en: There are fewer shoppers than usual in the supermarket, and two chains have already cut back on big discounts.

teaser.text: הסופרמרקטים מרגישים ירידה בתנועה, ושינויי הנסיעות של אנשים משפיעים גם על המבצעים.

translations.ru: Супермаркеты ощущают спад трафика, а изменения в поездках людей влияют и на акции.
translations.en: Supermarkets are feeling a drop in traffic, and people’s travel plans are also affecting promotions.

teaser.text: למרות שהחג קרוב, יש פחות עומס מהרגיל, וכמה רשתות כבר מצמצמות הנחות כדי לשמור על רווחיות.

translations.ru: Хотя праздник уже близко, загруженность ниже обычной, и некоторые сети уже сокращают скидки, чтобы сохранить прибыльность.
translations.en: Even though the holiday is close, traffic is lighter than usual, and some chains are already cutting discounts to keep margins.

sources.title: Israel to add iodine to household salt, citing risks to child development

The article is useful for ordinary Hebrew because it involves buses, operators, regulation, service obligations, and the practical effects of transport disputes on riders.

The story centers on Frankfurt as a creative person and explains how work, design choices, and manufacturing shaped her public impact.

sources.title: Dorin Frankfurt at Ashdod Museum of Art

stories.brief: The Jerusalem Post’s Dorin Frankfurt profile describes decades of Israeli garment making, including a South Tel Aviv factory that employed workers from many communities. A tenant is organizing a shared freezer in the building’s common kitchen after someone left several bags in the wrong section. The tenant asks a neighbor whether the top shelf is still free, but the neighbor says they already put two boxes there for a weekend dinner. After a quick check, they notice one bag is leaking and another has no name on it, so they separate the items and put labels on the containers. The neighbor agrees to move one box to their own apartment freezer, and the tenant clears enough space for everyone’s essentials. In the end, the freezer is usable again, nobody loses food, and they decide to keep a simple label sheet nearby.
